note: Researched recommendations, written in the site's voice but by somebody who has not been. Opinionated on purpose — a list of facts is not a guide — but every card says plainly that it was researched rather than visited, and a handwritten note in notes.json overrules any of it. This file exists because nothing else can fill it: no open dataset in India describes everyday food, Wikidata holds two Delhi restaurants and no cafes, and the whole sourced tier here is monuments. See SOURCES.md.
rules: Every record needs a source and a lastVerified date. If it cannot be checked, it does not go in.
Say what to order and when to go. 'Lovely atmosphere' helps nobody.
No opening hours in prose. OpenStreetMap carries them, js/hours.js reads them, and a time written here is a time that rots.
quality and uniqueness cap at 4 here. 5 is reserved for somewhere one of you actually loved.
Where a claim is disputed, say it is disputed. Delhi has more than one restaurant claiming to have invented the same dish and at least one of those arguments is in court.

Always pin `match` with a zone. Matching on name alone resolved 'Bukhara' to a restaurant in Noida rather than the one in Chanakyapuri — and the famous one is not in OpenStreetMap at all, so the record was dropped. That is the index doing its job: it is what stops a writer inventing a place.

items.title: Karim's
items.why: Founded in 1913 near the Jama Masjid by Haji Karimuddin, whose family had cooked for the Mughal court, and often called Old Delhi's most famous place to eat. The menu is Mughlai: nihari, kebabs, korma, biryani.

items.title: Moti Mahal
items.why: The Daryaganj restaurant Kundan Lal Gujral opened after Partition, one of the first to bring Punjabi food like tandoori chicken, dal makhani and butter chicken to a wide audience. Order the tandoori chicken.

items.title: Indian Accent
items.why: Rohit Khattar's modern Indian restaurant, opened in 2009 at The Manor and at The Lodhi hotel since 2017, with sister restaurants in New York and Mumbai. Book well ahead for the tasting menu.

items.title: Saravana Bhavan
items.why: The Connaught Place branch of the Chennai-based South Indian vegetarian chain, which has grown to dozens of outlets in India and abroad. Come for a dosa and filter coffee.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Lodhi Gardens
items.why: Ninety acres with eleven monuments standing in it — the tombs of Muhammad Shah Sayyid (1444) and Sikandar Lodi, the Bada Gumbad, the Shish Gumbad — laid out as a garden around them in 1936. Delhi walks here in the morning. The octagonal Sayyid tomb is the one to look at properly: Hindu features built into an Indo-Islamic building.
items.source: Wikipedia; Incredible India; position confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Sunder Nursery
items.why: Ninety acres next to Humayun's Tomb, derelict for decades and reopened in 2018 after a ten-year restoration by the Aga Khan Trust for Culture — the charbagh canals rebuilt, the axis to the tomb restored, hundreds of native species planted as Delhi's first arboretum. Six World Heritage monuments stand inside it. Time put it on its list of the world's hundred greatest places that year.
items.source: Wikipedia; Aga Khan Development Network; Delhi Tourism; position confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Agrasen ki Baoli
items.why: A historical stepwell, 60 metres long and 15 wide, set among the office blocks off Hailey Road near Connaught Place. Go on a quiet weekday morning.

items.title: Bahrisons Booksellers
items.why: The Khan Market bookshop Balraj Bahri Malhotra opened in 1953 after Partition, raising the money by selling one of his mother's gold bangles. Still run by the family.

items.title: Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters
items.why: A Khan Market café of the Gurugram-based roaster, which buys from more than eighty Indian coffee estates and smallholders. Ask what single estate is on the bar.

items.title: Bengali Sweet House
items.why: A sweet shop in Bengali Market, one of New Delhi's oldest markets, built in 1930 by Bengali Mal Lohia — the name has nothing to do with Bengal. Buy a box of sweets to take away.

items.title: Khari Baoli Spice Market
items.why: Asia's largest wholesale spice market, trading since the seventeenth century by the Fatehpuri Masjid at the western end of Chandni Chowk, selling spices, nuts, herbs, rice and tea. Go early.

items.title: Lajpat Nagar Central Market
items.why: The central market of Lajpat Nagar, the South Delhi neighbourhood named after Lala Lajpat Rai. Clothes, fabric, shoes and household goods; evenings are busiest.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); Delhi Tourism; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Nai Sarak Bookshop Area
items.why: Nai Sarak, the 'new street' between Chandni Chowk and Chawri Bazaar, is a wholesale and retail market for school and college textbooks. Walk it after a paratha in the lane next door.

items.title: Wenger's
items.why: One of the first shops in Connaught Place. It began in 1926 at Kashmere Gate, run by a Swiss couple who introduced Delhi to pastries and Swiss chocolates, and still bakes its own breads and cakes.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: L'Opera
items.why: A French bakery near Khan Market that makes its own viennoiserie, macarons, pastries and breads. Stop for a croissant or a box of macarons.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Cafe Lota
items.why: The café inside the National Crafts Museum, opposite Purana Qila, cooking regional Indian food. See the museum first, then have lunch.
items.source: National Crafts Museum; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Kunzum Travel Cafe
items.why: A Hauz Khas Village café built around books and travel, with its own book club and reading events. Come to read over a coffee.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Subko Cafe
items.why: The Lodhi Colony café of Subko, a specialty coffee roaster that also makes fine cacao and runs a craft bakehouse. Order a coffee and something from the bakery counter.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters
items.why: A Chittaranjan Park café of the Gurugram-based roaster, which buys from more than eighty Indian coffee estates and smallholders. Ask what single estate is on the bar.

items.title: Indian Coffee House
items.why: A branch of the Indian Coffee House, the chain run by worker co-operatives since the first outlet opened in Bombay in 1936. Cheap coffee and snacks in a room with history.

items.title: Bahrisons Booksellers
items.why: The Khan Market bookshop Balraj Bahri Malhotra opened in 1953, a refugee from Partition who sold a gold bangle for the capital. Still run by the family.

items.title: Another Fine Day

match.name: Another Fine Day Cafe and Reading Room

items.why: A café tucked into Gurugram's corporate blocks, with an all-day breakfast menu, mezze, grills, sandwiches and wraps. Good alone with a book or with company.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters
items.why: A Malviya Nagar café of the Gurugram-based roaster, which buys from more than eighty Indian coffee estates and smallholders. Ask what single estate is on the bar.

items.title: Moti Mahal Delux
items.why: A branch of the chain descended from Kundan Lal Gujral's Moti Mahal in Daryaganj, the restaurant credited with popularising tandoori chicken, butter chicken and dal makhani. Order those.

items.title: United Coffee House
items.why: One of Connaught Place's early restaurants, where Jawaharlal Nehru came to hear the poet Josh Malihabadi at its mushairas. Continental and Mughlai food in an old-fashioned room.

items.title: The Big Chill
items.why: The Khan Market home of Delhi's Big Chill café chain, which now runs three places in the market including its own cakery. Italian food, long dessert list.

items.title: Guppy
items.why: AD Singh's Japanese-themed restaurant in Lodhi Colony, from the restaurateur behind Olive. Book for dinner.

items.title: Colocal
items.why: A chocolate maker selling bars made from Indian-origin cacao, like its 55 per cent single-origin dark, plus cookies and coffee. Buy a bar to take home.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: One8 commune
items.why: A branch of One8 Commune, the chain of restaurant-bars started by cricketer Virat Kohli. A big, easy room for a drink near the airport.

items.title: Chache di Hatti
items.why: The Kamla Nagar chole bhature shop that draws very long queues during its short opening hours. Get there early.

items.title: Kallu Nihari
items.why: A shop in Old Delhi that has served nothing but nihari, a slow-cooked meat stew, since Mohammed Rafiquddin — Kallu Mian — opened it in 1990. Go early; it sells out.

items.title: Arsalan Restaurant & Caterer
items.why: The Delhi branch of Arsalan, the Kolkata restaurant known for its Kolkata-style biryani. Order the biryani.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Farzi Cafe
items.why: A Cyber Hub branch of Farzi Café, one of Zorawar Kalra's modern Indian restaurant brands. Good for a group dinner.

items.title: Ladurée
items.why: The Khan Market shop and tearoom of Ladurée, the Paris pastry house founded in 1862 on the rue Royale and best known for macarons. Buy a box to take away.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Game On Board
items.why: Delhi's first board-game café, with a library of more than 500 games and game masters to teach them, plus food and drink. Bring friends and stay a few hours.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Piano Man New Delhi
items.why: The Eldeco Centre stage of The Piano Man, Delhi's best-known jazz club, with live music most nights. Book tickets for the show you want.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Big Chill
items.why: The Kailash Colony café of the Big Chill, Delhi's own café chain. Italian food and a long dessert list.

items.title: The Big Chill
items.why: The Saket branch of the Big Chill, Delhi's own café chain. Italian food and a long dessert list.

items.title: L'Opera
items.why: A Vasant Vihar shop of L'Opéra, the French bakery making its own viennoiserie, macarons, pastries and breads. Stop for a croissant.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Call Me Ten
items.why: A Japanese restaurant in Basant Lok, opened in 2024 by a group of founders including actor Neha Sharma. Good for sushi and small plates at dinner.

items.title: The Big Chill
items.why: The Vasant Kunj branch of the Big Chill, Delhi's own café chain. Italian food and a long dessert list.

items.title: Kwality
items.why: One of the early Connaught Place restaurants, which brought Continental and Mughlai cooking to the plaza. An old-fashioned room for lunch.

items.title: The Big Chill
items.why: The Connaught Place branch of the Big Chill, Delhi's own café chain. Italian food and a long dessert list.

items.title: Devan's at Lodhi
items.why: A Lodhi Colony shop of Devan's, the coffee and tea merchant selling single-origin coffees, blends and teas from Darjeeling, Assam and the Nilgiris. Buy freshly ground coffee.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Jalebi Wala
items.why: The Old Famous Jalebi Wala at the Dariba Kalan corner of Chandni Chowk, frying crisp jalebis. Buy them hot, by weight.

items.title: Dhaba
items.why: Dhaba by Claridges, a restaurant themed on a Punjabi highway dhaba, cooking rustic North Indian food. Order dal and something from the tandoor.

items.title: Another Fine Day
items.why: A café in Gurugram's corporate blocks with an all-day breakfast menu, mezze, grills, sandwiches and wraps. Good alone with a book or with company.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap
